items.evidence: play --ticks 1 on a fresh place printed screen title and every key the brief names (tick, screen, menu_index ... stamps, records), with the no-season defaults.
--frame fr/X.png --size 800x480 wrote PNGs; IHDR reads 800 x 480 for title, slots, settings, morning, stall, paused, day, upgrades, evening, season_over.

Fresh title texts are right (no Continue), menu_index 0, Up at 0 and Down at 4 stop. But Quit (down x4, enter at tick 4) does not end the run: with --ticks 50 the state prints tick 50, and --at 5,6,20 shows the run going on. Words stop acting, but the run keeps ticking.
Settings start at English/Normal/7 days with the exact texts; Left/Right step es<->en, easy..hard, 7<->3 and clamp at both ends; Escape and Enter on Back go to title (tick 23 title).
Set es/easy/3 days in run 1 (folder k3); run 2 on k3 started language es, difficulty easy, length 3. A fresh folder gave en/normal/7, slots [null,null,null], stamps [], records [].

In Spanish, texts on title, records, stamps, slots, settings, morning, stall, day, paused, evening, upgrades and season_over were all Spanish (Ajustes, Manana, Puesto, Pasillo, Tarde, Mejoras, Bancarrota...). The settings screen changed to Spanish on the same tick as Right. en.json and es.json have the same keys.
modules/work/strings/en.json and es.json hold all strings; README 'Adding a language' explains the steps (one include line in lib.rs plus a lang.xx key).
Fresh place, Enter on New season: texts [New season, Slot 1: Empty, Slot 2: Empty, Slot 3: Empty]; Escape went back to title.
Seed 1 slot 1: screen morning, day 1, slot 1, coins 50, reputation 50, stock all [], prices 4/6/11/14/7/9, upgrades [], crate_limit 8, order null, texts Morning, Day 1 of 7, Coins: 50.

Easy started with 60 coins and Hard with 40. A 3-day season said Day 1 of 3 with forecast [sun,sun,cloud]. After changing the setting hard->normal and continuing, season_difficulty stayed hard and the rent was 30.

Forecasts have 7 (or 3) entries, all from sun/cloud/rain/heat. Weather and 'Weather: Heat/Sun/Cloud' follow the day (seed 6: day 3 cloud, day 4 sun, day 5 heat). The same seed gave the same forecast, other seeds gave others.
Wholesale for seeds 1-7 and later days were all in range (for example apples 1-4, fish 6-9, honey 4-7). Rows read like 'Apples: 4 a unit, stock 0'.
Enter on Apples at 4: coins 50->26 and stock [{units 6, days_left 5}]; second lot gave coins 2 and one batch of 12; row 'Apples: 4 a unit, stock 12'. Honey batch days_left null; fish 2, bread 1.
With 2 coins, Enter on Bread changed nothing and added 'Not enough coins', which went away at the next word. I could not reach the 99-unit cap: the most I could buy was 48 apples with 151 coins.
Day 1 order null. Day 2 seed 4: order {cheese, 4, pay 66 = 4*11*3/2}, text 'Order: 4 Cheese for 66'. accept -> taken true, 'Order taken: 4 Cheese for 66'; a second accept changed nothing.
After a season was started then given up, a later run's title read [Day Market, New season, Continue, Records, ...] and Continue slots showed 'Slot 1: Day 1 of 7, 50 coins'.

In a later run with --seed 77, Continue slot 1 opened day 6 with the saved coins 165, stock, prices 12/33, stall, upgrades, forecast, wholesale and order (honey 6 for 81). Enter on an empty slot 2 changed nothing.

Escape on Morning, Stall and Day gave paused [Paused, Resume, Title]. The clock stood at 38 from tick 300 to 351. Escape/Resume returned to the same screen, menu and state. Title kept the slot at 50 coins with no stock, even though 12 apples had been bought.
Stall opens with cursor (0,0), apples selected, and texts Stall, Good: Apples, Price: 4, Stock: N (6/12/48 as stocked), Crates: 0 of 8.
Down/Left at (0,0) stayed; Up went to y 1 and stopped; Right x5 went to x 5 and stopped; Down went back to y 0.
prev_good from apples gave honey; next_good cycled apples, bread, cheese, fish, flowers, honey, apples. Good/Price/Stock texts followed (Price 6, 11, 14, 7, 9).

put added {x 5,y 0,apples} with Crates 1 of 8; put on the occupied cell did nothing; take removed it; take on the empty cell did nothing. With 8 crates a 9th put did nothing. Stall listed by x then y.
Ten price_up from 4 stopped at 12; twelve price_down stopped at 1; 'Price: N' followed.
Stall layout and prices (apples 12, cheese 33) carried from day 5 to day 6, and were the same after Continue in a later run.
Enter on Stall: screen day, clock 0, speed slow, texts include 08:00 and Speed: Slow, taken/served/walked_out/passed 0, visitors list present.
verify.py over 4 days: ids 1.., minutes strictly increasing within 0-479, types valid, distinct wants of 2/1/2/3. Seed 6 gave the same list twice; seed 7 gave a different one.

--at: slow went 0->1 after 20 ticks; fast every 5; hold froze the clock at 4 for 20 ticks with screen day; rush went +1 per tick. Progress carried over (slow after rush reached clock 8 at the predicted tick). Time and Speed texts followed.
finish at tick 108 gave evening at tick 109 with clock 480. Its output hash was identical to the same day run at rush (keys taken, served, walked_out, passed, sales, coins, reputation, texts, stock).
The same day at finish, rush, fast (2600 ticks), slow (9800 ticks) and a fast/hold/slow/rush/finish mix all had the same evening hash: taken 400, served 37.
verify.py over 4 full days at rush (every minute): each visitor was on the aisle at x = clock - m for m..m+5 and off it from m+6. No errors.

verify.py: every take came from the column's front crate, or from the back crate only when the basket was already non-empty; only wanted goods, none taken twice. Without Sign, a back-row-only apples crate sold 0.
Apples crate at column 0. Price 4: cooks held 2 apples at 4 from clock m with budget_left 32. Price 5: cooks took none. Tourists took 1 at 6 (budget_left 14) and none at 7.
verify.py: no take with units*price above budget_left, and units held in aisle and queue baskets never exceeded stock, over 4 days.
verify.py: visitors leaving with an empty basket raised passed by exactly that many; those with goods were queued (joined m+6) or at a till that minute.

verify.py: every service had ends = start + 2 + goods in basket. Payment came at ends with bargain less a tenth; coins and taken rose by the amount paid. 124 sales checked; served and rep rose; stock fell; sales entries correct.

Seed 3 clock 99: till ended visitor 14 and took queued visitor 15 the same minute (ends 102). verify.py: a till was never free while the queue was non-empty, and visitors leaving the aisle went straight to a free till.

No queued visitor ever waited at or over its patience across ~2400 simulated minutes. But the queue never passed 2, walked_out stayed 0 in every run, and the walk-out path (goods back, rep -2, walked_out +1) was never seen.
Seed 6 day 3: visitor 87 was on the aisle at clock 479. At evening, aisle/queue/tills were [] and passed (49) and walked_out (0) were unchanged.
With Second till, tills had 2 entries. Both tills were busy at once in 5 minutes. Of 27 starts with both tills free, all went to till 1.
Same day, apples only in back crate (0,1): with Sign, apples sold 12 / taken 48; without Sign, sold 0 / taken 0.
Taken order 8 cheese with 12 in stock: 'Order delivered: 132', coins 66+132-33=165, cheese 12->4. Taken 4 cheese with none: 'Order failed', reputation 50->45. An untaken order changed nothing.
Bread bought day 1 (no crate): 'Bread: sold 0, spoiled 6', spoiled 6. Fish bought day 1 had days_left 1 that evening and was spoiled 6 on day 2's evening. Honey stayed {6, null}.
Heat day without Cool box: apples days_left 5->3. Heat day with Cool box: apples 4->3, cheese 6->5.
Rent 24 = 20+2*2 at Normal; 15/17/23/25 at Easy with 0/1/4/5 crates; 30 at Hard with 0 crates. 'Rent: N' shown and subtracted.

Evening texts: Evening, Day N of 7, Taken/Served/Walked out/Passed matching state, six good lines matching sales and stock, Rent, Coins, Reputation, 'Tomorrow: Sun/Heat/Cloud' from the next forecast entry.
Enter on Evening gave Upgrades [Upgrades, Coins: 386, Next day, Second till: 80, Cool box: 40, Sign: 30, Extra crates: 50, Awning: 35]. Next day opened Morning day+1.

Buying all five took 80/40/30/50/35 and each row read 'owned'. Enter on an owned row kept coins at 23. With 30 coins, Second till showed 'Not enough coins'. Extra crates made crate_limit 12 and 'Crates: 7 of 12'.

In-run: coins -6 -> 'Bankrupt', slots [null,null,null], Season over 'Bankrupt','Score: 0', record bankrupt true. But the kept slot was never cleared: settings.json still held slot1, and the next run showed Continue and 'Slot 1: Day 2 of 7, 9 coins'.

In-run, the 3-day Easy season was right: 'Season over', 'Score: 486' (386+100), 'Days: 3', 'Best: 486', and no Continue. A later run on the same place showed Continue again, with 'Slot 1: Day 3 of 3, 201 coins' still in the kept file.

After 7 ended seasons, records were [486, 65, 0, 0, 0] (5 kept, best first). A later run's Records read 'Score 486, 3 days, Easy' ... 'Score 0, 2 days, Hard, bankrupt'. Fresh Records said 'Aun no hay records' / no-records line.

'Stamp: First coin','Stamp: Sold out' showed on day 1's evening only; later evenings showed only new ones. stamps were in brief order. The Stamps screen in a later run read 'First coin: yes', 'Full stall: no', and so on.
First coin on the first day with a sale. Full stall on a day opened with 9 crates (with Extra crates). Whole season on day 3 of a 3-day Easy season with coins 386.
Sold out earned when crated apples (12 at open) sold to 0. Not earned when fish had stock but no crate (seed 4 day 1), or when flowers had crates but 0 stock at open.
Day 6 played unbroken and day 6 played after Continue in a later run (seed 77) gave byte-identical visitors, sales, stock and evening. Caveat: prices were set high, so that day had no sales.
Two runs, seed 6, same script, from separate copies of the same kept folder, printed identical output (same md5). Seed 7 gave a different hash, forecast, wholesale and visitor list.
Escape on Evening, Left on title, put on Morning, and accept/finish/rush on Stall all left the state unchanged.

goods.json, visitors.json and market.json (rates, weather, difficulties, upgrades, stamps and their thresholds) are included as data. README 'Changing data' says how to change each; what an upgrade or stamp does stays code keyed by id.
fr/stall.png: 6x2 grid; six goods in distinct colours where stall says (front row apples..honey, back (5,1) apples); white cursor at (3,1); text shows Good: Apples, Price: 4, Crates: 7 of 8.

fr/day.png: stall crates, tourist T17 (yellow) on aisle cell 0, regular R16 (blue) at the till, text with 09:37, Speed: Rush, Coins 128, Taken 113, Served 10, Reputation 100. The queue was empty in this frame.

Title, slots, settings, morning, upgrades, paused and season_over frames show their texts with '> ' on the chosen row. The evening frame (three different runs, by finish and by rush) shows only the literal '{work.disp}' and none of the Evening texts.
README gives how to play, where kept things are (--settings folder, keys prefs/slot1-3/stamps/records), and play/frame commands that ran as written.

defects: Several words at the same tick act only once (0:down,0:down,0:down gave menu_index 1); the brief requires each to act in order. README admits this.
A season that ends (bankrupt or finished) is cleared from the slot in memory, but the kept slot keeps the last Morning save. A later run offers Continue and replays the ended season.
The Evening frame renders the placeholder '{work.disp}' instead of the evening text.
Quit freezes input but does not end the headless run; tick keeps counting to --ticks.
A 'none' word does not clear 'Not enough coins' unless it releases a held word (README admits).
could_not_check: d14: the 99-unit cap needs more than 99 units of one good bought; the most reachable was 48 units in the runs I made.
d37: no visitor ever walked out of the queue in any run (queue never exceeded 2), so the walk-out effects could not be seen.
